source.title: Velocitune: A Velocity-based Dynamic Domain Reweighting Method for Continual Pre-training
source.authors: Zheheng Luo; Xin Zhang; Xiao Liu; Haoling Li; Yeyun Gong; Chen Qi; Peng Cheng

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present. Some figure and table layout is flattened, but the scaling-prediction error table is readable.
record.tranche_reason: Applies a scaling law in the new setting of domain-adaptive continual pre-training and reports errors for predicting full-dataset evaluation loss from checkpoints through half the training data.
record.gate_note: The paper reports average scaling-law prediction errors in Table 6, recorded below. Downstream benchmark results concern the proposed domain-reweighting method and are not results on scaling-law predictability or downstream predictability from scale. Scaling-law results cited from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper applies the Chinchilla law as a tool to set per-domain target losses for its Velocitune reweighting method. Table 6 is a sanity check of that tool, not a test of any version. Each fit uses checkpoints within one continual-pretraining run, through about half the data, and predicts the loss at the full data only 2x further. Errors are averaged over domains, with no loss scale, baseline or uncertainty. So they cannot show power-law form over orders of magnitude (V1), extrapolation orders of magnitude out (V2), or that the power-law form holds in a new regime (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase covers only the appendix error table. The authors' main conclusion is different: Velocitune reweights domains by learning velocity during continual pretraining. It beats proportional-weight baselines on math, code (CodeLlama-7B) and CmdGen (Llama3-8B, Mistral-7B). Ablations show the predicted target loss and data ordering both matter. The scaling-law fit is presented as a cheap way to estimate target losses without a proxy model.
record.recipe_differences: Fits a scaling law to checkpoint evaluation losses in continual pre-training and predicts full-dataset losses; the paper does not provide enough detail here to establish that its fitting procedure matches the original studies exactly.
record.method_sensitivity: The prediction setup uses checkpoints saved through half the training data; no comparison of alternative fitting choices is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: A Chinchilla-form law was fitted to checkpoint eval losses through half the data in continual pretraining of 7-8B models. Its predicted full-data loss has average error 2.4e-3 (Reasoning) and 1.84e-3 (SystemStack).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Chinchilla-form fits to within-run learning curves in domain-adaptive continual pretraining predict end-of-run per-domain loss to within a few thousandths (2x token extrapolation).

record.problems: The prediction errors are reported only as aggregates over domains; SystemStack's model or models are not identified in Table 6. The reported prediction setting covers half-to-full training data, not extrapolation over several orders of magnitude. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these errors.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling-related rows were omitted. Downstream benchmark scores and domain-weight results were left out because they do not measure the scaling-law claims.
record.verdict_notes: The proxy sample ratios in Table 8 are 58% (SystemStack) and 51% (Reasoning), roughly consistent with 'half the training data'. The record's V2/V5 limits_scope labels are withdrawn: a 2x within-run extrapolation of an assumed law is tool validation, not a test.

versions.untested_parts: Does not report power-law loss trends or exponents across parameters, tokens or compute over several orders of magnitude.
Tests prediction from checkpoints through half the training data to the full dataset, not predictions across orders of magnitude or to much larger models.
Does not study compute-optimal parameter and token allocations.
Does not compare architecture details at fixed parameter count.
Tests loss prediction in continual text pre-training only; does not test other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning or transfer.
Does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitting choices, exponents or compute-optimal splits, or report curves bending away from a power law.
